newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says takes Japan to WTO over satellite contract.
newsitem.headline: EU says takes Japan to WTO over satellite contract.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it would take Japan to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) for excluding European suppliers from a satellite navigation system contract.
The Commission said Japan had required bidders for the $40 million government contract to use U.S. technical specifications, contrary to provisions of the WTO Government Procurement Agreement (GPA).
"The European Commission has decided to request formal consultations with Japan in the WTO," it said in a statement.
Formal consultations is the first step in the WTO's dispute resolution procedure.

When the Japanese Ministry of Transport issued a call for tender last November for components for a global navigation system for aeroplanes, it specifically referred to U.S. technical specifications called WAAS, the Commission said.
That effectively excluded specifications known as EGNOS that were developed by the European Global Navigation Satellite System, it said.

"If left unchallenged, this could set a damaging precedent for the development of the world market in a key area of technology where European firms are some of the most competitive in the world," it said.
The Commission said the tender violated GPA provisions on transparency and non-discrimination.
